facts.statement: Anasazisaurus is a saurolophine hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur that lived approximately 74 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Anasazisaurus ( ; "Anasazi lizard") is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid ("duckbill") ornithopod dinosaur that lived about 74 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Anasazisaurus have been found in the Farmington Member of the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: It was found in the Farmington Member of the Kirtland Formation, in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: To date, only a partial skull has been discovered for Anasazisaurus.
facts.quote: Only a partial skull has been found to date.

facts.statement: Anasazisaurus is known for a short nasal crest that projected above and between its eyes.
facts.quote: It is known for its short nasal crest, which stuck out above and between its eyes for a short distance.

facts.statement: American paleontologists Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas named the dinosaur Anasazisaurus in 1993.
facts.quote: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas, American paleontologists, named this dinosaur in 1993.

facts.statement: The holotype skull, the only known specimen of Anasazisaurus, was collected in the late 1970s by a Brigham Young University field party and is cataloged as BYU 12950.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (and only known specimen) was collected in the late 1970s by a Brigham Young University field party working in San Juan County, and is housed at BYU as BYU 12950.

facts.statement: Anasazisaurus possesses a unique bone flange rising from the nasals between and above the eyes that folds back under itself.
facts.quote: It has a sort of tab or flange of bone, from the nasals, that rises between and above the eyes and folds back under itself.

facts.statement: The maximum preserved length of the Anasazisaurus skull is approximately 90 centimeters.
facts.quote: The maximum preserved length of the skull is ~90 centimeters (~35 in).

facts.statement: According to Gregory S. Paul, Anasazisaurus was about 7.5 meters long and weighed up to 2500 kilograms.
facts.quote: According to Gregory S. Paul, it was about 7.5 meters long and weigh up to 2500 kg.

facts.statement: Anasazisaurus is classified as a saurolophine hadrosaurid, a group characterized by lacking a hollow crest.
facts.quote: Anasazisaurus is a saurolophine hadrosaurid, meaning it lacked a hollow crest.

facts.statement: As a hadrosaurid, Anasazisaurus was likely a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore with a skull capable of a grinding motion analogous to chewing.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Anasazisaurus would have been a large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating plants with a sophisticated skull that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing.

facts.statement: Anasazisaurus had teeth that were continually replaced and packed into dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at any time.
facts.quote: Its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Anasazisaurus likely fed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters high.
facts.quote: Feeding would have been from the ground up to ~4 meters (13 ft) above.

facts.statement: The geological formation containing Anasazisaurus fossils dates to the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 73 and 74 million years ago.
facts.quote: This formation dates from the late Campanian stages of the Late Cretaceous Period (73-74 million years ago),

facts.statement: It is debated whether Anasazisaurus is a valid genus; some researchers, including Thomas Williamson and Alberto Prieto-Marquez, argue it should be classified as a species of Kritosaurus (Kritosaurus horneri).
facts.quote: However, others disagreed, including Thomas Williamson, who made the most detailed published case. In a paper published in 2014, Alberto Prieto-Marquez agreed that Anasazisaurus horneri is similar to Kritosaurus navajovius, but found it distinct enough to be considered a valid species of Kritosaurus, as K. horneri.

facts.statement: The Spanish Wikipedia entry classifies Anasazisaurus within the subfamily Saurolophinae.
The Kirtland Formation where Anasazisaurus was found is dated to the late Campanian of the Upper Cretaceous, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Anasazisaurus as the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
